data.title: Cathie Wood Says TSLA Holders ‘Will Get’ A Premium If SpaceX Buys Tesla — HSBC Puts It At Over 30%
data.description:
Key points:
  • HSBC models a 33% premium, valuing Tesla at $507 a share in a deal or $212 on its own.
  • Wood sees Tesla’s robotaxis helping fund SpaceX’s orbital data centers.
  • A deal could reportedly be announced in December and would need backing from holders of 50% of Tesla shares.

If SpaceX wants Tesla shareholders to approve a buyout, ARK Investment Management CEO Cathie Wood believes it will have to offer them a premium, and HSBC estimates that a bid 33% above Tesla’s 30-day average would value the stock at $507 per share.

“We do think the Tesla shareholder will demand a premium and will get a premium, whether it’s going to be 25% or what have you. I think it’s going to be worth it to SpaceX,” Wood told CNBC’s Squawk Box on Friday.

While neither company has announced an offer, Tesla shareholders would have considerable say over any deal. Elon Musk told investors in October that a merger would need the backing of holders of 50% of all outstanding Tesla shares. Even a majority of the votes cast could fall short.

HSBC Puts Tesla Buyout At $507 Per Share 

The prospect of a SpaceX bid changed how HSBC values Tesla stock. “Given the acquisition newsflow, we believe the current share price of Tesla offers an anchor, irrespective of the fundamentals,” the bank said in a note.

Drawing on premiums paid in comparable deals, HSBC estimated that a bid 33% above Tesla’s 30-day average would value the stock at $507 a share. If Tesla stays independent, the bank values it at $212 a share based on the cash it expects Tesla’s seven businesses to generate. HSBC gave the two outcomes equal weight and more than doubled its price target to $359 from $157, implying a 4% upside from current levels, while upgrading the stock to ‘Hold’ from ‘Reduce.’

Wood Makes The Case For A Tesla Premium 

Meanwhile, Wood sees a role for Tesla’s robotaxis in one of SpaceX’s most expensive ambitions. “In the short-term, RoboTaxi is going to deliver massive cash flows, we believe, which will help fund orbital data centers,” she said. Wood expects computing in orbit to become cheaper than computing on Earth within two years. In a stock-for-stock deal, Tesla investors would own a piece of the business their robotaxis could help finance.

ARK owns both stocks and has run the numbers from each side of the table. In October, its researchers estimated that a premium of about 24% to Tesla’s closing price at the time would divide the projected gains from a merger evenly between the two groups of shareholders.

The companies already have an elaborate business relationship. Tesla booked $626 million in revenue from sales of its Megapack batteries to SpaceX in the first nine months of 2026. Additionally, billionaire investor Chamath Palihapitiya sees a broader opportunity in bringing their power supplies, chips, AI models, and products under one roof. At SpaceX’s Starbase in Texas, Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas flagged a computing campus of more than one gigawatt, according to a note shared by Tesla investor Sawyer Merritt.

HSBC Sees Control As Musk’s Main Motive 

HSBC also sees a clear incentive for Musk in a potential merger. SpaceX’s share structure gives him more voting power than he has at Tesla. “We see control as the key motivation for a merger, especially as CEO Musk has been clear in the past about his need for oversight,” the bank said.

Independent directors at both companies are weighing a possible deal. Musk said his role at each company keeps him out of those talks. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he told investors on SpaceX’s earnings call last month. SpaceX and Tesla could reportedly announce a merger as early as December, though the announcement could slip into early 2027.

Baron Sees Gains With Or Without A Merger 

On the other hand, Ron Baron, a longtime shareholder in both Tesla and SpaceX, declined to say what price would win his vote. “Whatever their decision is, I’m going to support him,” Baron said in a CNBC interview.

Baron said his investments in Musk’s companies had already earned about $30 billion and could generate hundreds of billions more over the next decade. When asked whether the gains depended on Tesla and SpaceX joining forces, he replied, “Doesn’t matter to me. He’s going to do what’s best for the companies and for operating most efficiently.”

How Do Retail Traders Feel About TSLA And SPCX?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘neutral’ on Tesla and ‘bearish’ on SpaceX at the time of writing, with ‘low’ message volume for both stocks.

One user said the talks could lift Tesla stock after Friday’s selloff: “SpaceX merger discussions remain a potential game-changing catalyst.”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said that the price should come first. “Tesla needs to determine a fair price for its agreement to the SpaceX merger.”

View this Stocktwits post

So far this year, Tesla shares are down 23%, while SpaceX shares are 5% below their June IPO price.

data.title: ConocoPhillips To Sell Norway Business, Stake In UK Teesside Oil Terminal To Vr Energi
data.description:
HOUSTON (dpa-AFX) - Energy major ConocoPhillips (COP) announced Monday a definitive agreement to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the U.K. Teesside oil terminal to Vr Energi.

The total consideration would be $4.425 billion, less agreed upon adjustments of approximately $0.5 billion as of the January 1, 2026, effective date.

Total consideration is expected to be $3.9 billion, including the remaining 2026 tax liability of approximately $1.4 billion, payable in the first half of 2027, resulting in net cash proceeds of around $2.5 billion.

The deal is expected to close by the end of the first quarter 2027, subject to approval by the Norwegian Ministry of Energy and regulatory conditions.

The sale includes ConocoPhillips Skandinavia AS and ConocoPhillips (U.K.) Teesside Operator Limited, which together hold the company's Norway and Teesside assets and associated decommissioning liabilities.

The Norway business includes ConocoPhillips' interests in producing assets on the Norwegian continental shelf, as well as interests in eight partner-operated fields across the Norwegian Sea and northern North Sea.

In 2025, the Norway business produced around 120 thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day. The year-end 2025 proved reserves associated with the sale

properties were approximately 221 million barrels of oil equivalent.

At the deal closing, Vr Energi will assume the post-effective date balance sheets of the properties.

ConocoPhillips plans to utilize proceeds for general purposes and for discretionary share repurchases in 2027 to supplement its long-standing commitment of

returning around 45% of cash from operations to shareholders.

Andy O'Brien, president and chief executive officer, said, 'Norway and Teesside are high-quality assets with strong operating histories, and we believe this win-win transaction unlocks value for ConocoPhillips while positioning these assets for continued success under new ownership.'

COP shares closed Friday's regular trading on the NYSE at $136.12, up 0.84%, while it lost 0.82% in the after-hours activity.

data.title: Bureau Veritas Acquires Topo Solutions; Strengthens AI-Powered Supply Chain Intelligence Offering
data.description:
PARIS (dpa-AFX) - Bureau Veritas SA (BVI.PA), a France-based testing, inspection and certification services provider, on Monday announced that it has acquired Topo Solutions, an AI-enabled digital supply chain management platform.

The company said that the acquisition will strengthen its AI-powered supply chain intelligence offering.

The deal will also expand its data-driven services and digital solutions for consumer goods companies and retailers worldwide.

The company said that the acquisition is aligned with its LEAP 28 strategy to accelerate growth in strategic markets through bolt-on acquisitions.

Topo Solutions is headquartered in Hong Kong, connects brands and retailers with suppliers, factories and service providers through a single platform.

The company generated approximately 3 million euros in revenue in 2025.

data.title: Smith & Nephew Names Nick Alexos as Next Finance Chief
data.description:
(07:00 GMT) *Smith & Nephew to Appoint Nick Alexos as CFO
(07:02 GMT) *Smith & Nephew: Alexos to Join on Nov. 30
(07:03 GMT) *Smith & Nephew: Alexos Was Most Recently CFO at Univar Solutions
(07:16 GMT) Smith & Nephew Names Nick Alexos as Next Finance Chief

By Adria Calatayud

Smith & Nephew said it would appoint Nick Alexos, a former executive at chemicals distributor Univar Solutions and dental-products supplier Dentsply Sirona, as its next chief financial officer.

The U.K. medical-technology company said Monday that Alexos would join as CFO and board member on Nov. 30.

The company said in August that its previous CFO, John Rogers, would leave at the end of September.

Alexos was most recently CFO at Univar, joining in 2020 when the company was listed on the New York Stock Exchange and staying after Apollo Global took it private in 2023. He was previously CFO and chief administrative officer of Dentsply Sirona between 2017 and 2019.

Smith & Nephew said Alexos would be based in the U.S. and travel widely.

data.title: NQ: Nasdaq Futures Rebound 3% After Brutal Week, Asian Markets Seek Support
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nasdaq rebounds after 10% weekly drop
  • Asia equities get government support
  • Gold, Bitcoin rally as dip buyers show up

US futures and gold recover as authorities move to steady Asian stocks. AI financing concerns keep investors cautious.

📈 Futures bounce after a bruising week

  • Nasdaq-100 futures rose 3% in Monday’s Asian session, while S&P 500 futures gained around 2%.
  • Buyers are returning after last week’s rout, although the recovery still leaves substantial losses to repair before sentiment can look more settled.
  • Friday’s cash session explains the scale of that task. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 5.3%, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Dow lost 1.9%. The Nasdaq suffered its worst week since March 2020, while the S&P and Dow confirmed corrections — declines exceeding 10% from their record closing highs.
  • Anthropic remains a key stock to watch. The newly listed company closed Friday at $88.91, down 8.5%, after touching $83.05, almost its $83 IPO price.

🌏 Asian authorities try to steady stocks

  • Taiwan’s benchmark recovered 2%, while South Korea’s Kospi remained around 2.5% lower after trimming deeper losses. European futures were steady and Japan was closed for a holiday.
  • Policy support is becoming more visible. Taiwan tightened short-selling rules, Chinese exchanges eased margin-financing requirements and South Korea reiterated its readiness to stabilize markets.
  • Those measures may help trading conditions, but investors still need reassurance that enormous AI infrastructure investments can generate adequate returns.
  • The dollar and government bonds largely retained Friday’s defensive gains. The euro remained below $1.10, while USDJPY briefly traded above ¥159.
  • Gold climbed 2.4% to $3,615 after losing about 9% last week, while silver gained 3% to $42.41. Bitcoin traded near $62,000 after touching a one-year low of $55,000 during thin weekend trading.

data.title: Smith+Nephew to appoint Nick Alexos as Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Smith+Nephew (LSE: SN, NYSE: SNN), the global medical technology business, announces Nick Alexos will join the company as Chief Financial Officer and the Board as an Executive Director on 30 November 2026.

Nick brings more than 35 years of financial, commercial and transaction experience, with a strong track record of driving operational performance and creating value from complex situations across global businesses and private equity.

Nick was most recently Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer at Univar Solutions, a global distributor of chemicals and ingredients (2020-2026). He joined Univar Solutions when it was listed on the NYSE (UNVR) and played a central role in delivering the company’s operational transformation. In March 2023, Apollo Global announced it was acquiring Univar Solutions in an $8 billion take-private transaction, which resulted in the Company delisting in 2023. Subsequently Nick continued his work supporting the operational improvement of the business as Chief Financial Officer, and also had responsibility for Univar Solutions’ on-line service business.

Previously, Nick was Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Administrative Officer of dental technology business Dentsply Sirona (2017-2019). As part of a new leadership team, he worked alongside the CEO to reshape the business to improve performance, including programmes focused on capital expenditure, inventory and cost control.

Prior to Dentsply Sirona, Nick spent 30 years at private equity firm Madison Dearborn Partners. As a Managing Director, he co-led 18 platform investments and was responsible for more than $14 billion of debt financings. His portfolio included multiple healthcare investments.

Rupert Soames, Chair of the Board, said: "Nick is an accomplished finance leader with deep experience across global businesses, public markets, private equity and capital markets. His track record in strategic transformation, M&A, financing and disciplined capital allocation will be highly valuable and we look forward to welcoming him to the Board."

Deepak Nath, Chief Executive Officer, said: "I am delighted to welcome Nick to Smith+Nephew. He brings strong financial and commercial leadership and has helped multiple businesses deliver significant value across his career. I look forward to working with him as we continue to sharpen execution, strengthen performance and deliver our strategic priorities."

Nick Alexos said: "I am excited to be joining Smith+Nephew, a global medical technology business with a strong heritage, leading positions in growing markets and significant potential. I look forward to working with Deepak, the Board and colleagues across the company to build on the progress already made and create sustainable value for our stakeholders."

Nick holds an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and a BBA/CPA in Accounting / Finance from Loyola University, Chicago. He will be based in the United States, but is expected to travel widely.

Emily Heaven, Smith+Nephew+44 (0) 7811 919437

Remuneration

The Remuneration Committee considered the remuneration arrangements for Nick and agreed the following standard arrangements:

  • Base salary: $900,000 per annum
  • Annual Incentive Plan: Target opportunity of 107.5% of base salary (maximum 215% of base salary)
  • Performance Share Plan: Target opportunity of 150% of base salary (maximum 300% of base salary)
  • Restricted Share Plan: 125% of base salary
  • Shareholding requirement: 300% of base salary
  • Pension and benefits in line with those available to other US employees.

In line with our standard practice for new hires during the year, Nick will also receive a pro-rata 2026 Restricted Share Plan award and a pro-rata 2026-28 Performance Share Plan award.

All arrangements are in line with the approved Director’s Remuneration Policy. Full details will be disclosed in the Directors' Remuneration Report for the relevant year.

There are no further matters required to be disclosed under UKLR 6.4.8R in respect of this appointment.

About Smith+Nephew

Smith+Nephew is a portfolio medical technology business focused on the repair, regeneration and replacement of soft and hard tissue. We exist to restore people’s bodies and their self-belief by using technology to take the limits off living. We call this purpose ‘Life Unlimited’. Our 17,000 employees deliver this mission every day, making a difference to patients’ lives through the excellence of our product portfolio, and the invention and application of new technologies across our three global business units of Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT and Advanced Wound Management.

Founded in Hull, UK, in 1856, we now operate in around 100 countries, and generated annual sales of $6.2 billion in 2025. Smith+Nephew is a constituent of the FTSE100 (LSE:SN, NYSE:SNN). The terms ‘Group’ and ‘Smith+Nephew’ are used to refer to Smith & Nephew plc and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless the context requires otherwise.

data.title: Julius Baer Assets Under Management Rise 6% In First 10 Months; Adj. Pre-tax Profit Up 17%
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Julius Baer Gruppe AG (JBAXY.PK, JBARF.PK, JGE.F, BAER.SW) Monday said that its Assets under Management, or AuM, rose 6 percent to 553 billion Swiss francs in the first ten months of 2026. During the same period, adjusted pre-tax profit was up 17 percent.

The Swiss banking and financial services company said that this 6 percent growth was mainly due to market performance, the appreciation of the US dollar against the Swiss franc, and net new money inflows of 8.5 billion francs. Every month, average AuM increased by 9 percent to 538 billion francs, compared to the year-ago period.

Julius Baer said that adjusted profit before taxes for the first ten months of 2026 was around 1.3 billion francs, up 17% from the underlying result of the same period of 2025. Gross margin was 82 basis points in the 10 months, compared with the underlying gross margin of 83 bps in the first ten months of last year

Julius Baer said that it launched a share buyback programme of up to 600 million francs on November 2 and it is expected to be completed within one year.

Looking ahead, based on its performance during the first ten months, the company expects IFRS and adjusted net profits for fiscal 2026 to be substantially higher than last year's results.

On the Swiss Exchange, BAER.SW ended Friday's trading at 65.38 Swiss francs, down 2.62 francs or 3.9 percent.

By Adam Whittaker

U.S. oil company ConocoPhillips said it agreed to sell its Norwegian oil and gas business, and a stake in a U.K. oil terminal, to Var Energi in a roughly $3.9 billion deal.

ConocoPhillips said Monday that it would receive around $2.5 billion in cash, with the Norwegian oil and gas company paying the remaining 2026 tax liability of approximately $1.4 billion, due in the first half of 2027. The sale includes a 40.25% interest in, and operatorship of, the U.K. Teesside oil terminal, ConocoPhillips said.

The cash will be used for general purposes and share repurchases in 2027, ConocoPhillips said.

The Norwegian assets produced around 120,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in 2025. In a separate release, Var Energi said the deal was accretive to earnings and dividend per share.

The deal is expected to close by the end of the first quarter next year.

data.title: HDFC Bank can double in 4 years; IT and consumer stocks offer value: Renaissance’s Pankaj Murarka
data.description:
HDFC Bank is positioned to compound at a 20% annual growth rate over the next four years, effectively doubling in value, according to Pankaj Murarka, Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer at Renaissance Investment Managers.

The broader Indian equity market is currently in the initial phase of a new upward leg following nearly two years of consolidation. Strong corporate earnings and a reversal of foreign outflows are driving this momentum. Investors remain underweight on India, creating a classic template for a market spike when combined with robust economic resilience.

Largecap banks remain a primary focus for the firm. HDFC Bank stands as its largest holding, followed by ICICI Bank, with the portfolio encompassing four of India's top five lenders, including Kotak Mahindra Bank. While the sector experienced a slow period previously, lenders are now delivering high-teens earnings growth—a trend expected to persist for at least the next two years.

"My view still remains that over the next four years, the stock can easily compound at 20% CAGR from here, which effectively means the stock can double over the next four years," Murarka noted regarding HDFC Bank. The underlying franchise remains rock solid and is trading significantly below its long-term averages, leaving room for further valuation catch-up.

Beyond financials, extreme market polarisation is prompting sharp sector rotations. Capital is exiting highly valued segments such as precision engineering, defence, artificial intelligence (AI) and capital goods. Funds are instead rotating into information technology (IT) services and consumer stocks, which are currently trading at attractive or reasonable prices on a cycle-adjusted basis.

A moderation in global commodity prices is expected to further accelerate corporate earnings growth in the second half of the current year, 2026-27 (FY27) and into 2027-28 (FY28). Because India is a net commodity importer, cooling prices will alleviate the margin pressures that consumer and auto companies have faced in recent quarters.

Addressing Tata Steel's acquisition of a stake in APL Apollo Tubes, the transaction makes strategic sense from a medium to long-term perspective given the significant opportunities in downstream steel. While the buyer may have slightly overpaid in the short term, acquiring strategic assets often requires a premium. The deal also provides a highly lucrative exit for APL Apollo's promoters.

On the macroeconomic front, the global economy must reconcile with a 5% risk-free rate on the United States dollar as the new normal, which will lead to a repricing of assets globally. Domestically, the acceleration of bilateral free trade agreements (FTAs), including with the European Union, will significantly de-risk the Indian economy.

data.title: Continental proposes closing South African tyre plant in Gqeberha, putting 950 jobs at risk
data.description:
German tyre maker Continental has proposed closing its tyre plant in Gqeberha, South Africa, putting about 950 jobs at risk in a move the Nelson Mandela Bay Business Chamber said would, together with earlier closures, effectively wipe out tyre manufacturing in the Eastern Cape.

Continental said on 20 November that it had begun a formal consultation under Section 189A of South Africa's Labour Relations Act to explore alternatives and measures to limit the impact on employees. If no viable alternative is found, operations at the site could be discontinued by early 2027, the company said in a statement.

The company cited underutilisation of local production capacity that had not improved over several years despite extensive turnaround efforts, compounded by price competition from low-cost imports, rising energy costs, supply chain disruptions and fragile infrastructure. Most employees will not report for normal shifts but will continue to be paid until 20 January 2027, according to a letter to staff cited by The Herald.

The plant has made tyres since 1947 and Continental-branded tyres since 1985. Continental's local sales organisation will continue to serve customers in South Africa and the region from Gqeberha, and its BestDrive retail network is unaffected.

'We are deeply concerned by the initiation of a Section 189A process relating to a proposal to permanently close Continental's manufacturing plant in Nelson Mandela Bay, potentially placing 950 jobs at risk,' chamber chief executive Denise van Huyssteen said.

The proposal comes 17 months after Goodyear NASDAQ:GT announced the closure of its plant in Kariega, affecting at least 907 jobs. ContiTech Africa launched a process in early 2025 to close its Kariega conveyor belt operation, and Bridgestone TSE:5108 shut its local plant in 2020.

'The cumulative impact of these closures effectively wipes out tyre manufacturing in the Eastern Cape, leaving only two tyre manufacturing facilities in South Africa, located in Brits and Ladysmith,' Van Huyssteen said, adding: 'South Africa is increasingly unable to compete with low-cost manufacturing countries, while our policies and responses are too slow to keep pace with the rapid changes in the global economic environment.'

The Motor Industry Staff Association (Misa) urged Continental to exhaust every avenue to keep the factory open. Its chief executive of operations, Martlé Keyter, said the Eastern Cape had the country's highest official unemployment rate, at 44.3% in the third quarter, against a national rate of 33.7%, Business Day reported.

data.title: Copper One Announces Option to Acquire 100 Percent of the Quatum Copper Project in British Columbia
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

Vancouver, BC – TheNewswire - November 23, 2026 – Copper One Resources Corp. (“Copper One”) (CSE: CEXY | OTCID: CEXYF | FSE: IW8 | WKN: A42AGR) (the “Company”) announces that it has entered into an option agreement dated November 20, 2026 with an arm’s-length vendor to acquire an undivided 100% interest in the Quatum Copper Project (“Quatum” or the “Project”), northeast of Campbell River, British Columbia. The Project comprises 12 mineral claims covering 3,646.90 hectares (approximately 9,011.7 acres) and two pending mineral claim applications covering an additional 746.86 hectares (approximately 1,845.5 acres). Together, the claims and applications cover 4,393.76 hectares (approximately 10,857.2 acres).

Quatum is located near the Company’s 100%-owned Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project on West Redonda Island. The historical CAP showing in the Quatum area lies approximately 13 kilometres (8 miles) north-northeast of the RED occurrence at Redonda. This proximity provides an opportunity to evaluate coordinated exploration planning and regional logistics, while building on Copper One’s experience at Redonda.1

David Greenway, President and Chief Executive Officer of Copper One, commented: “Quatum represents an exciting opportunity for Copper One to advance a copper-bearing breccia system previously explored by Newmont. Its historical drilling and surface mineralization provide a compelling foundation for renewed exploration using modern techniques. Its proximity to our ongoing drilling at the 100%-owned Redonda Project, previously explored by Teck, strengthens the strategic fit and creates opportunities to apply our regional geological knowledge and coordinate exploration activities. Together, these projects expand our presence in British Columbia and reinforce our strategy of building a substantial North American copper portfolio. With projects across Nevada, Utah and British Columbia, Copper One is assembling multiple opportunities for discovery and growth as the world’s need for copper continues to expand.”

Quatum Project highlights

  • Government records document three diamond drill holes completed by Newmont in 1970, totaling 2,410 feet (approximately 735 metres).


  • Historical copper mineralization associated with an intrusive breccia system near the CAP showing, with chalcopyrite and locally observed bornite.


  • Historical Hole 1 results include 0.17% copper over 100 feet (30.48 metres), with a higher-grade interval of 0.38% copper over 10 feet (3.05 metres). These are historical reported results requiring verification.


  • Historical surface chip sampling at location J returned a reported weighted average of 0.46% copper over 20 feet (6.10 metres). True widths are unknown.


  • Historical mapping, soil sampling and geophysical surveys provide a basis for evaluating targets for follow-up exploration.


Historical exploration and geological setting

The British Columbia Geological Survey identifies the CAP or QUATUM RIVER showing as a copper showing classified as a porphyry copper occurrence hosted by intrusive rocks of the Coast Plutonic Complex. Its description records chalcopyrite, pyrite and pyrrhotite mainly within a breccia pipe hosted by quartz monzonite and quartz diorite.2

British Columbia’s Geology, Exploration and Mining 1970 (p. 229) records three surface diamond drill holes totalling 2,410 feet (approximately 735 metres) on the Cap 2 claim, together with geological mapping, 6.6 line-miles (approximately 10.6 line-kilometres) of magnetometer and induced polarization surveys, and 296 soil samples.3

A November 16, 1970, memorandum by M.F. Cowan reports the following drill observations and results. Hole 1 was drilled at azimuth 226° and inclination −25°; Hole 2 at 250° and −25°; and Hole 3 at 190° and −25°.4

Hole

2

3

Disseminated sulphides observed from 455–490 ft (138.68–149.35 m). No copper assay is provided for this interval.

Cowan recorded bornite in Hole 1 and identified untested material above the drill intersections and anomalous soils toward Burma Creek. He also described a smaller, structurally bounded breccia footprint than earlier mapping suggested. A subsequent January 28, 1971, memorandum by W.R. Bacon concluded that the drilling had not justified further work at that time. These differing historical interpretations require reassessment.5

Cowan’s June 17, 1970, summary tabulates surface chip samples at location J averaging 0.46% copper over 20 feet (6.10 metres), including 0.93% over 5 feet (1.52 metres). The report identifies this as surface sampling; it has not been verified as a trench intersection.6

The Transaction

To exercise the option to acquire an undivided 100% interest, Copper One must pay a total of C$800,000, including the C$20,000 signing deposit, issue 900,000 common shares and incur C$500,000 in minimum property expenditures, according to the following schedule. All amounts are in Canadian dollars.7

Excess expenditures may be carried forward. The Optionors are to act as operator for the first two years. The agreement provides for transfer of title after the second-anniversary payment, to be held in trust until the option is exercised; beneficial vesting follows satisfaction of the option requirements.

The agreement is subject to a 3% net smelter returns royalty, with the right to purchase one-half of that royalty (1.5 percentage points) for C$1.5 million.

Historical information and data verification

The historical exploration information is drawn from government publications and archived reports and memoranda prepared in 1970 and 1971. It is presented to explain the basis for further investigation and is not current verified exploration data. Drill lengths are downhole lengths, surface results are sample lengths, and true widths are unknown. Visual sulphide observations, including bornite and chalcopyrite, do not establish copper grade or economic significance. Float is transported material and may not represent the underlying bedrock.

The records reviewed do not provide a complete set of drill assay certificates, collar coordinates, sampling and recovery records, analytical procedures or quality assurance and quality control documentation. Broader drill-interval endpoints and the relationship of historical workings to present claim boundaries remain to be confirmed. Historical sample sites and drill collars require field verification; additional sampling and potentially drilling will be needed to test the reliability and continuity of the reported mineralization.

Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information contained in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Larry Segerstrom, M.Sc. (Geology), CPG, a non-independent consulting geologist to the Company and a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects.

About Copper One Resources Corp.

Copper One Resources Corp. is focused on identifying, acquiring and advancing high-potential copper, copper-silver-gold and copper-molybdenum projects to help meet global demand for critical metals used in electrification, AI infrastructure and data centres, renewable energy, defence and power system modernization.

The Company's flagship asset is the Majuba Hill Copper-Silver-Gold District, located approximately 156 miles (251 kilometres) from Reno, Nevada. Majuba Hill is an exploration-stage porphyry copper project situated in an established mining jurisdiction with existing infrastructure, where ongoing exploration is focused on evaluating the scale and continuity of a copper-silver-gold mineralized system.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Redonda Copper-Molybdenum Project, located northeast of Campbell River in British Columbia's Vancouver Mining Division. The district-scale project comprises approximately 2,746.46 hectares (6,787 acres) across nine mineral claims and hosts a porphyry-style copper-molybdenum system within the Coast Suture Zone, a geological belt known for porphyry copper and skarn mineralization. Systematic exploration is continuing to evaluate the scale and continuity of the mineralized system.

In addition, Copper One holds an option to earn up to a 100% interest in the Redhill Property, located south of Ashcroft, British Columbia, adjacent to the Trans-Canada Highway. The 4,736-hectare (11,703-acre) property hosts volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) mineralization prospective for copper, zinc, silver and gold, while also demonstrating potential for epithermal gold mineralization.

Copper One also owns a 100% interest in the Sport Project in Utah through its wholly owned subsidiary, Rooinek Mining Corp., expanding the Company’s portfolio of North American copper exploration assets.

Copper One is advancing its portfolio through systematic exploration, modern geological modelling and disciplined technical evaluation. The Company remains committed to responsible exploration practices, technical transparency and the disciplined advancement of critical-metals projects across North America.

    Vancouver, BC – TheNewswire - November 23, 2026 – Uranium One Mining Corp. ("Uranium One" or the "Company") (UUU: CSE | UUUFF: OTCID | SL5: Frankfurt) is pleased to announce the appointment of Jeremy S. Brett, M.Sc., P.Geo., as a technical advisor. Mr. Brett has been involved with the Company’s recently acquired Pasfield Lake Uranium Project in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin for more than two decades. He will draw on that experience to advise the Company on reviewing historical exploration records and planning future exploration of the project.

    Mr. Brett’s technical and exploration background Includes:

    • More than 30 years of international mineral exploration experience as a Senior Geophysical Consultant, in all geophysical methods and most commodities on five continents

    • Consulting experience with more than 100 leading junior and major exploration and mining companies, as well as provincial and national governments, in Canada and internationally

    • M.Sc. in Geology (Geophysics) and B.Sc. in Physics (Geophysics) from the University of Toronto

    • Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) registered with Professional Geoscientists Ontario

    • Extensive experience consulting to and directing geophysical and geological exploration programs

    • Uranium experience in Athabasca-type and other uranium settings in Canada and internationally

    • Served on the board of directors of the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC)

    • Expertise in integrating geophysical, geological and physical-properties data with ore deposit models and structural geology to identify and test exploration targets

    David Greenway, Chief Executive Officer of Uranium One, commented: “Jeremy’s appointment brings valuable technical expertise and more than two decades of familiarity with Pasfield Lake to Uranium One. His experience integrating geophysical and geological data will help guide our evaluation of the project’s extensive historical exploration database and refine priorities for future exploration. As we advance our Athabasca Basin portfolio, we are focused on building the technical foundation needed to identify and systematically test compelling uranium targets.”

    Biography

    Mr. Brett is a Senior Geophysical Consultant who has designed, supervised, quality-assured and interpreted exploration programs for uranium, copper and a broad range of other commodities in North, Central and South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East. He has advised more than 100 junior and major exploration and mining companies, as well as provincial and national governments. He has also served as the geophysics champion for the PDAC Exploration Assessment Digital Data Formats working group. His experience includes exploration program design, project management, data integration, target prioritization and target testing. He is familiar with the reporting requirements under National Instrument 43-101.

    Mr. Brett specializes in integrating geophysical, geological and physical-properties data with ore deposit models and structural geology to identify and test exploration targets. He is a Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) registered with Professional Geoscientists Ontario. He is a Fellow of the Society of Economic Geologists (SEG) and a member of the Canadian Exploration Geophysical Society (KEGS), Professional Engineers & Geoscientists Newfoundland & Labrador (PEGNL), and the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC).

The resistance is at $4.53-3/4, a break above which may lead to a gain into the range of $4.55-3/4 to $4.59. On the daily chart, a wave (3) is still unfolding toward $4.40-1/2, the 461.8% projection level.

The market is likely to stabilize in the support zone of $4.40-1/2 to $4.41 and bounce.

data.title: Gold Touches Buy Levels, With $4,200 as Next Key Resistance on Charts — Market Talk
data.description: Gold touches buy levels during Asian trading, Maybank analysts say in an FX research and strategy report. "Democrats' agenda to bring the cost of living down, undo [President] Trump's tariffs and end the war are all disinflationary efforts that could be more benign" to gold, the analysts say. Also, a growth slowdown for the U.S. and even the rest of the world could provide a macro backdrop for a shift in expectations for the Fed to ease monetary policy, which might attract more eager buyers of the precious metal, the analysts say. Based on technical charts, gold's next key resistance is around $4,200 a troy ounce, the analysts add. Spot gold is 2.4% higher at $3,622.34 an ounce. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
